name: workflow
description: Backlog-driven work loop in one plugin. /backlog writes one backlog item and gets its acceptance criteria approved; with --survey it researches the repository and the outside with parallel agents, has a separate judge agent filter the candidates (the collectors have only read, web and note-writing tools, the judge only read and web tools), and shows them with draft acceptance criteria. /start takes one backlog item, or a task you describe on the spot, from plan to merge in one run: baseline, stack checks, implementation, deslop, verification, acceptance criteria checked only with outside evidence or a separate judge, review with code-review plus the stack reviewers, valid findings fixed without asking, then one final message for the decisions only the user can make and the merge. Claude invokes both on its own when you ask to add or start a backlog item. It asks only about irreversible or outward actions, shared config changes, product or taste decisions, choosing what to do, and states that could lose work; everything else is decided and logged with the reason and the cost of being wrong. There is no plan approval. Say run until done and it stops only for the merge and irreversible actions. Every agent it launches reads a worker rules file first: the brief's bar is the whole bar, do not ask a person, report what you chose. Both skills open a sub-session by default for backlog items (start in its own worktree on a w/ branch); --here, or no session tool, runs in the current session. The start skill carries a when-to-what index over 24 principles, 16 skills (architect, figure-it-out, blast-radius, how, why, a project verification skill with a feature map, control-ui, control-cli, deslop, no-comments, verify-this and more) and 8 playbooks (investigation, feature, bug-fix, refactoring, prototype, perf-issue, hillclimb, opening-a-pr) adapted from pstack and cursor-team-kit, read when they apply and invocable by name. Stack checks run only when the item touches their area: frontend (Svelte and React references that hand general rules to the official Svelte, Vercel React and React Router skills and the Next.js bundled docs, scripts that start the dev server on the item port and check added lines for debug code and dependency changes for the lockfile, the ui-design skill for DESIGN.md and design canvas mockups, the frontend-reviewer and design-reviewer agents, and the frontend-evaluator agent that verifies acceptance criteria in the browser) and server (Node.js servers and Supabase: migrations, RLS, keys; config keys, committed value files and keys checked by a script; the api-reviewer and supabase-reviewer agents, which hand general Supabase and Postgres rules to the official Supabase skills). /kit-setup writes per-role model and effort choices (sub-sessions, implementing, review, judge, mechanical fixes, exploration) to a JSON file the skills read and installs the official skills and plugins that fit the project stack, and /kit-help answers how to use the plugin. Installs are not asked about: it uses what the item or plan names, or picks a proven one and reports it. Fix-and-recheck loops stop and hand over after three failed fixes of the same criterion. A Stop hook re-runs the base branch's verify command when an item is marked done (and says so if the branch changed it), also after another Stop hook such as /goal has blocked. Web and server ports are split per item. Mechanical steps run as tested scripts: picking a free item port, and running the branch's new tests against the base branch's source to flag tests that do not prove the fix.
